messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details:
The failing test `skipUsingRead()` verifies the behavior of the IOUtils.skip() method when used on an InputStream where the skip() method always returns 0 (simulating a stream that cannot skip forward).

The current bug report highlights an issue relevant to this test: IOUtils.skip() does not adhere to its documented contract stating that the method "will only skip less than the requested number of bytes if the end of the input stream has been reached." The failure occurs because the current implementation of skip in IOUtils calls input.skip(numToSkip) in a loop and breaks the loop immediately if skip returns zero:

```java
long skipped = input.skip(numToSkip);
if (skipped == 0) {
    break;
}
numToSkip -= skipped;
```

This is evident in the snippet from IOUtils.skip():
- At line 97, it calls `input.skip(numToSkip)`.
- At line 98-99, if skipped bytes is zero, it breaks the loop.
- Then returns the total bytes effectively skipped.

If there is an InputStream whose skip() method returns zero (like the FilterInputStream subclass in the test), but is not actually at EOF, this will cause premature termination of skipping and thus the skip() method in IOUtils returns a result smaller than expected. This violates the contract, because the method declares it will only skip less when EOF is reached, but in fact it may stop skipping early if skip() returns zero once for other reasons.

The failing test wraps the stream so skip always returns 0, simulating this problematic case. Hence the test fails because IOUtils.skip() returns that it skipped zero bytes immediately, even though it should keep reading/skipping until EOF or requested bytes are skipped.

The root cause: IOUtils.skip() relies exclusively on `InputStream.skip()` and interprets a zero skip as EOF or end of skipping, while some InputStream implementations (e.g., ciphered streams or wrapped streams) may have skip() always returning 0 and require fallback logic such as reading and discarding bytes one-by-one or in blocks to effectively skip.

No evidence in recent bug reports contradicts or supplements this diagnosis directly, so the primary explanation stands: IOUtils.skip() is incorrectly implemented and does not handle the zero skip result properly.

Hence the bug is that IOUtils.skip() does not provide a robust skip implementation for InputStreams whose skip method behaves in this way (returns 0 even though more bytes can be read).

Next step: IOUtils.skip() should implement fallback logic that attempts to use read() to skip bytes if skip returns zero, until it truly detects EOF. This will allow handling edge cases like the filter stream in the test and the CipherInputStream described in the bug report.

This diagnosis fully explains why the test `skipUsingRead()` fails and the discrepancy between the IOUtils.skip contract and observed behavior in the reported real-world case.
